packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 14

Only the packet prompt, metadata and supplied images were consulted. No work/author identification, catalogue or prior transcription was consulted or exposed.

Layout survey
Both photographs show a bound opening containing a broad manuscript strip. The strip's writing is upside down in the supplied images. It has four compact text columns, two on each side of a central fold, and a very broad blank area. Thin horizontal and vertical rules are visible; the horizontal rules, especially on image-002, should not be mistaken for lemma underlining. The hand is brown, small and very heavily abbreviated. No colored rubrics, decorative initials or running title can be securely identified. Some capitals or paragraph marks are slightly larger. A short differently oriented note appears in image-001's blank area; its reading and function remain unresolved. Other, larger-script book leaves are visible behind/below the strip in both photographs, oriented differently. They are separate surfaces and were not combined with the strip's text or used to infer identification. The two strip photographs show distinct faces, not simple duplicate crops.

Selection and coordinates
Rotated the strip by 180 degrees for inspection. No confident heading is present. Selected two adjacent columns of image-002, where ruling and letter outlines are clearest. Even here I cannot recover two useful continuous passages; the samples below record only uncertain fragments in physical sequence.

For unambiguous ORIGINAL-image labelling, columns A–D are numbered LEFT TO RIGHT AS SUPPLIED, before rotation. Thus the selected original D is the leftmost column after rotation, and original C is next to it. Physical line numbers count from the TOP OF THE ORIGINAL IMAGE in each column. Since the writing is upside down, reading order within these samples proceeds from higher numbered to lower numbered lines. Approximate original y coordinates are included. Baselines at the binding fold are excluded; they do not affect the counts from the original top.

These proposed groups are explicitly low-confidence and are not sufficient to support a source match. “Calidum?” in particular is only a tentative shape reading, not a content inference. No abbreviation expansion is proposed. No definite textual deletion or interlinear insertion was recognized. Apparent overlap with ruled lines is not treated as cancellation.

Transforms
Original image-001: 5000×3333; image-002: 5000×3169. Overview strip crops: image-001 (200,833)–(4850,2599), image-002 (200,697)–(4850,2249), each rotated 180 degrees. Detail crops of image-002: (3220,1330)–(4190,2090) and (2290,1330)–(3220,2140), also rotated 180 degrees and inspected at native scale. No filtering, contrast manipulation, sharpening or reconstruction. Detail crops repeat the overview lines and were not counted as extra text.

Limitations and unread areas
Most of the strip, its differently oriented note, and all background leaves remain untranscribed. The photographs are detailed, but the heavily compressed hand exceeds my reliable reading in these selections. Perspective and fold occlusion complicate line counts, which are marked approximate. A specialist second image-only reading is needed; a flat perpendicular detail photograph could also help. No missing words were supplied from grammar or a possible source.
